title: Anacaona
note: Taíno cacica, poet, and composer of Jaragua (Hispaniola) who negotiated with early Spanish arrivals, resisted Spanish conquest, and was executed by hanging under Governor Nicolás de Ovando in 1503.

title: Hatuey's resistance in Cuba
note: Taíno cacique Hatuey mobilized warriors to resist Diego Velázquez's Spanish invasion of Cuba after fleeing Hispaniola, becoming one of the earliest recorded Indigenous anti-colonial resistance leaders in the Americas.

title: Establishment of the encomienda system on Hispaniola
note: Institutionalization of forced Indigenous labor distribution (repartimiento/encomienda) under Governor Nicolás de Ovando on Hispaniola, coinciding with the earliest documented arrival of enslaved Africans in the Caribbean in 1502.

title: Treaty of Tordesillas
note: Bilateral treaty between the crowns of Castile and Portugal establishing a global demarcation meridian 370 leagues west of Cape Verde to divide spheres of overseas exploration and imperial conquest.
